newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says German '97 deficit to be under 3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says German '97 deficit to be under 3 pct.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday he would ensure that Germany's 1997 budget deficit would be below three percent of gross domestic product, within the Maastricht treaty's target for European monetary union.

Speaking after Germany's six leading institutes said Bonn would post a budget deficit of 3.5 percent of GDP, Waigel said "the necessary decisions will be met in the final negotiations over the 1997 budget."
"The federal government will continue on its strict consolidation course," Waigel said in a statement.
"It will create the conditions for the state deficit to be below three percent of GDP in 1997," he added.

Waigel has little time to find further savings after the Free Democrats, the junior partners in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government stood in the way of tax increases to plug holes which have opened up in state finances.
Parliament's budget committee meets on November 14 to work out a final draft before submitting it for parliamentary approval.
